commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): skill usage stats, concurrency-safe approval, review audit, browse page

Follows a review of two proposed skills-taxonomy architectures (LTREE
hierarchy, microservice, Elasticsearch, embeddings) -- assessed as
overkill at current scale (~180 skills, ~100 postings/month) and
skipped. Ported the 3 items with real value: usage stats, a
concurrency fix for the one genuine risk in the current approve flow,
and a review audit trail. Plus a frontend page, since there was no way
to see the taxonomy at all before this.

skill_usage_stats table + record_skill_usage() (app/understanding/
taxonomy/candidates.py): every draft's matched required/preferred (or
primary) skills increment times_seen/last_seen_at for that canonical
name. Called once per draft in app/channels/service.py, same best-
effort/non-blocking pattern as the existing taxonomy-candidate
recording beside it.

add_canonical_skill (app/understanding/taxonomy/loader.py) now wraps
its read-modify-write of canonical_skills.json in a Postgres
transaction-scoped advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock). Two
approvals landing at the same moment -- two admins, or one double-
click -- previously both read the file before either wrote it back,
silently discarding the first approval. The lock releases on its own
when the transaction ends, so there's no matching unlock call to
forget, and it's safe across the connection pool since it's scoped to
whichever connection the transaction happens to run on.

reviewed_by added to taxonomy_candidates (ALTER TABLE, additive to the
existing table). approve_taxonomy_candidate/reject_taxonomy_candidate
take it; the moderation router passes the authenticated user's id.

New GET /understanding/taxonomy/skills/browse -- canonical skills
merged with usage stats, a separate endpoint from the existing
/taxonomy/skills/canonical rather than changing that one's response
shape (other callers may already depend on its exact contract).

Frontend: new SkillsTaxonomyPage -- searchable, filterable by category,
sortable by most-used/recently-seen/name. "Skills taxonomy" in top nav.
This is the first place the taxonomy is actually visible in the UI;
before this it was only reachable by reading canonical_skills.json
directly on the server.

New coverage: usage stats accumulate across separate record_skill_usage
calls: a skill repeated within one call counts once, not twice
(matches a real draft mentioning the same skill in both required and
preferred sections); approving the same skill twice doesn't duplicate
it or deadlock the advisory lock against itself. Full regression suite
(18 checks) green against a freshly built image and freshly reset
schema. Frontend type-checks and builds clean.
